nodes.summary: For $\beta > 0$, the Gaussian $\beta$-ensemble is the law on $\mathbb{R}^N$ with density proportional to $\prod_{i<j} |\lambda_i - \lambda_j|^\beta \exp(-\frac{\beta N}{4} \sum_i \lambda_i^2)$; for $\beta = 1, 2, 4$ it is the law of the eigenvalues of the GOE, GUE and GSE. Ben Arous and Guionnet proved that the empirical spectral measure $L_N = \frac{1}{N} \sum_i \delta_{\lambda_i}$ satisfies a large deviation…
nodes.title: Ben Arous–Guionnet large deviations

nodes.summary: Large deviation principles transfer along continuous maps: if $\mu_n$ satisfies an LDP with a good rate function $I$ and $F$ is continuous into a Hausdorff space, the image measures $F_*\mu_n$ satisfy an LDP with the good rate function $J(y) = \inf\{I(x) : F(x) = y\}$. Goodness of $I$ is what makes $J$ lower semicontinuous: the infimum is attained and the sub-level sets of $J$ are images of compact sets.
nodes.title: Contraction principle

nodes.summary: For i.i.d. random vectors with a finite moment generating function, the empirical means satisfy a large deviation principle whose rate function is the Legendre transform of the logarithmic moment generating function. The theorem is proved in $\mathbb{R}^d$ under a finite moment generating function: the upper bound by Chernoff bounds in half-spaces and exponential tightness, the lower bound by exponential tilting,…
nodes.title: Cramér's theorem

nodes.summary: The empirical measures $L_n = \frac1n \sum_{i<n} \delta_{X_i}$ of an i.i.d. sample with law $\alpha$ on a Polish space satisfy a large deviation principle in the weak topology with rate function $\beta \mapsto \mathrm{KL}(\beta \,\|\, \alpha)$: the probability that the sample looks as if drawn from $\beta$ is about $e^{-n \mathrm{KL}(\beta \| \alpha)}$. Cramér's theorem for means follows by the contraction…
nodes.title: Sanov's theorem

nodes.title: Gärtner–Ellis theorem (differentiable case)

nodes.summary: On a Polish space, a large deviation principle with a good rate function forces its measures to concentrate on compact sets up to exponentially small mass: for every $\ell$ there is a compact $K$ with $\mu_n(K^c) \le e^{-n\ell}$ for all $n$, the large deviation analogue of Prokhorov tightness. This is what reduces large deviation estimates to compact sets, and it gives the product principle: rate functions of…
nodes.title: Superexponential tightness and product LDPs

nodes.summary: Reweighting by an exponential of $n$ times a bounded continuous function preserves large deviation principles: if $\mu_n$ satisfies an LDP with rate function $I$, the Gibbs measures $Q_n \propto e^{nF}\mu_n$ satisfy an LDP with rate $J = \sup(F - I) - (F - I)$, which vanishes exactly at the maximisers of $F - I$. This is the large deviation form of the Gibbs conditioning and exponential tilting used in statistical…
nodes.title: Tilted large deviation principle

nodes.summary: The Laplace method for large deviation principles: if $\mu_n$ satisfies an LDP with rate function $I$ and $F$ is bounded and continuous, then $\frac1n \log \int e^{nF}\,d\mu_n \to \sup_x (F(x) - I(x))$. Logarithms of exponential moments are Legendre-dual to rate functions; this is the bridge from large deviations to free energies and variational formulas.
